messages:
maya: Heads-up — observed 3 OOMs on g4-cluster-3 in the last 40m, all during 512->1024 token spikes. Suspect allocator warmup + kernel-selector tuning from last deploy.
rohit: any stack traces or profiler snippets? can you paste the peak numbers?
maya: pasted profiler lines below. notice allocator reserves jump on first large request and doesn't shrink.
maya: ```
[profile] 2026-03-18T11:02:12Z model=lama-v2 kernel=fast_attn alloc_peak=11.2GB workspace_reserved=9.6GB kv_cache=1.1GB
[profile] 2026-03-18T11:02:12Z call=decode seq=1024 batch=1 latency=320ms
[profile] 2026-03-18T11:02:14Z oom during allocate(12.1GB) trace=alloc.cc:234
```
sylvia: allocator seems to pre-warm to max observed workspace. combined with kv coldstart/populate concurrency it exceeds node capacity. did kernel-selector change in yesterday's runtime deploy?
liam: yes — rolled kernel_selector.threshold_seq from 384 -> 512 in the rollout to favor fast_attn for longer sequences. also merged async-kv-populate which can run concurrent populates for multi-chunk requests.
rohit: that lines up. fast_attn has a large ephemeral workspace for fused kernels; async kv populate can overlap and double the transient peak.
maya: oncall-bot opened an incident: INC-20260318-2694 and paged oncall.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260318-2694 — PagerDuty notified :rotating_light:
liam: quick mitigation plan (hotfix):
1) revert kernel_selector.threshold_seq to 384
2) enable progressive allocator heatup that caps initial workspace to 60% of configured workspace and grows on stable allocation
3) reduce kv_cache.prefetch_parallelism to 1 for affected fleets
4) enable model-variant fallback for very large seqs (lama-v2-small) for non-SLA traffic
rohit: adding short-term circuit: if seq>512 && batch>1 -> route to protected lane with headroom reservation OR throttle to single inflight request. avoids simultaneous kv+workspace peaks.
sylvia: agree. also add runtime metrics: allocator.heatup_level, kv.concurrent_populates, kernel_selector.choice and alert when gpu_mem_util > 90% for >30s.
rohit: draft hotfix config I can push as a staged patch:
```yaml
runtime:
  allocator:
    heatup_mode: progressive
    initial_workspace_frac: 0.6
    max_workspace_frac: 0.85
  kernel_selector:
    threshold_seq: 384
  kv_cache:
    prefetch_parallelism: 1
    ttl: 5m
  fallbacks:
    large_seq_variant: lama-v2-small
    enable_circuit: true
```
maya: pushing staged rollout to 10% of g4-cluster-3 now (3 nodes). will observe for 15m and then expand if green.
liam: also add a per-request timeline capture: log alloc_peak_bytes and kv_populate_start/finish per request id to prove overlap in postmortem. we should have an alert that surfaces overlap events where alloc_peak + kv_peak > node_free_mem.
rohit: agreed. for the incident postmortem I'll collect the KV snapshot timeline + allocator peaks per req id. that's the evidence we need to show overlap created the OOM.
sylvia: if hotfix holds, plan to make progressive heatup default in the next minor. add a unit/integration test that simulates seq=1024 burst and validates allocator growth behavior.
maya: update: 12m into staged rollout — no new OOMs on the 3 nodes. telemetry shows initial_workspace_frac ~0.6 and kv.concurrent_populates=1. no kernel choices flipping to fast_attn for seq 512.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260318-2694 status -> mitigated
liam: great — next steps:
• expand rollout to 50% with monitoring on mem-util spikes
• run a synthetic burst test (seq=1024, batch=2, 20 reqs/s) in staging to exercise heatup path
• open PR to revert threshold permanently and add a guarded flag for fast_attn rollout with canary gating based on allocator metrics
rohit: i'll draft the postmortem with timeline + commits + remediation checklist. include rollback playbook and routing-circuit rules.
sylvia: nice containment. add security review for the config change before broad rollout (kv ttl change).
maya: ack. will follow-up with timeline and logs in the incident doc. thanks all.
